statement: Hemalurgy can transfer Allomantic or Feruchemical powers; its outcome depends on how and where the spike is used. This does not define a complete binding-point map.
implementation: PowerGrant stores the art, metal and source. Extraction and binding points are deferred.

statement: Represent each grant independently and retain its origin. Removing one source preserves unrelated grants. This is a data-model interpretation, not a complete account of spiritweb damage.
implementation: PowerGrant and Spiritweb.withoutSource; no spike insertion/removal gameplay.

statement: For the Phase 1 access display, use the strongest applicable grant. Preserve every grant so later canon research can revise stacking without losing provenance.
implementation: Spiritweb.strength; no additive strength or effect engine.

statement: Reserve distinct item and Identity UUIDs. An absent Identity field does not itself grant permission to tap an item. Charge units remain abstract pending the attribute engine.
implementation: MetalItemData persistence contract only. No Identity simulation or access-control gameplay.

statement: New characters begin without powers. Player spiritweb data copies on death; active effects are never persisted. Acquisition and death balance remain future design decisions.
implementation: Persistent Fabric attachment with copyOnDeath. No active-effect fields.

statement: God metals, precise alloy ratios, anatomical binding points, Compounding, Fortune, Connection and unsealed metalmind behavior require explicit evidence and documented interpretations before implementation.
implementation: No mechanics registered. Base catalog contains the sixteen standard metal IDs only.
